title: DNA Size Selection and Cleanup Using Optimized SPRI Beads
author: Miriam Schalamun
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.idmca46
materials: Make sure the beads are resuspend properly by flicking the tube gently and spinning it down - the solution will be homogeneous and brown (I put it in a 50°C Thermoblock for about 20 seconds to encourage the elution reaction)

steps.title: Prepare bead stock solution
steps.instruction: In a 50 mL tube combine 4.44 mL Milli‑Q water, 100 µL 10 mM Tris‑HCl (pH 8), 20 µL 1 mM EDTA (pH 8), 3.2 mL 1.6 M NaCl, 2.2 mL 50 % (w/v) PEG 8000, and 40 µL 0.4 % (v/v) Ser‑Mag SpeedBeads (GE Healthcare, PN 24152105050250). Vortex thoroughly; this 10 mL bead stock is ready for use.

steps.title: Initial bead washing
steps.instruction: Pipette 40 µL of the bead suspension into a 1.5 mL tube, place on a magnetic rack, wait until the solution clears and beads collect at the tube wall.

steps.title: Wash beads four times
steps.instruction: For each of four washes: remove the supernatant, add 1.5 mL Milli‑Q water, mix well, spin briefly in a microcentrifuge, return tube to the magnet, and wait for beads to re‑assemble at the wall.

steps.title: Add stock solution to beads
steps.instruction: After the final wash, remove the tube from the magnet, add 40 µL of the prepared 10 mL bead stock (step 1), mix, spin down, then transfer the entire contents back into the 50 mL stock tube and vortex.

steps.title: Add PEG to complete stock
steps.instruction: Add the remaining 2.2 mL of 50 % PEG 8000 to the 50 mL tube, vortex vigorously (pipette carefully because the solution is very viscous). The bead‑PEG stock is now ready.

steps.title: Adjust DNA sample volume
steps.instruction: Place your DNA sample in a 1.5 mL tube at a convenient volume (typically 20–200 µL). If the sample is highly viscous or contaminated, dilute and split into two tubes to improve handling.

steps.title: Add beads to DNA
steps.instruction: Add bead suspension at a volume equal to 1 × the sample volume (or 0.8 × to preferentially remove smaller fragments), using room‑temperature beads, and mix by flicking the tube.

steps.title: Incubate binding reaction
steps.instruction: Place the tube on a rotor or mixer and mix for 10 minutes at room temperature.

steps.title: Collect beads on magnet
steps.instruction: Spin the tube briefly in a microcentrifuge, place on the magnetic rack, and wait until the beads migrate to the wall and the solution becomes clear (1 min to >1 h). If beads remain cloudy, add an equal volume of buffer and beads, mix, and repeat the magnet step.

steps.title: Remove supernatant
steps.instruction: Discard the clear supernatant while the tube remains on the magnet.

steps.title: First ethanol wash
steps.instruction: Add 1–1.5 mL 70 % ethanol to the side opposite the bead pellet, wait 30 seconds, then discard the ethanol while the tube stays on the magnet.

steps.title: Second ethanol wash
steps.instruction: Without removing the tube from the magnet, repeat the addition of 1–1.5 mL 70 % ethanol, wait 30 seconds, then discard the ethanol.

steps.title: Final ethanol removal
steps.instruction: Take the tube off the magnet, spin briefly to collect residual ethanol, return to the magnet, and pipette off any remaining ethanol.

steps.title: Air‑dry beads
steps.instruction: Allow the beads to air‑dry for no more than 30 seconds; longer drying makes elution difficult.

steps.title: Elute DNA
steps.instruction: Add 50 µL (or desired volume) of 10 mM Tris (or TE) pre‑heated to 50 °C, mix gently, spin down, place on the magnet, and wait until beads re‑collect (typically 5–10 minutes, up to a few hours for very long DNA).

steps.title: Collect eluate
steps.instruction: When the solution is clear, pipette the supernatant (purified DNA) into a fresh tube and discard the beads.

steps.title: Quantify DNA
steps.instruction: Measure DNA concentration with a Qubit fluorometer; expected recovery for >20 kb HMW DNA is 60–90 %.

steps.title: Optional gel quality check
steps.instruction: Run a 0.8 % agarose gel loading 80 ng DNA per sample (normalized to 10 µL per lane) for 45 minutes in 1× TBE. Include lanes: control (untreated), 10 kb ladder, and samples prepared with 0.45×, 1×, 0.9×, and 0.8× bead volumes.
